  - button "Copy table":
  - heading "1. Plausible — my default recommendation" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - link "Plausible Analytics":
      - /url: https://plausible.io/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - text: Plausible Analytics
    - text: is probably the strongest starting point for most small SaaS companies. It is open source, uses no cookies or persistent identifiers, doesn't collect personal data, and hosts its cloud service on European infrastructure. Its dashboard is deliberately much simpler than GA4.
    - link "Plausible Analytics +1":
      - /url: https://plausible.io/privacy-focused-web-analytics?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Plausible Analytics
      - generic: "+1"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Choose it if:"
    - text: you mainly need traffic, acquisition channels, pages, goals/events and conversions without building an analytics operation.
  - heading "2. Fathom — polished and hands-off" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - link "Fathom Analytics":
      - /url: https://usefathom.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - text: Fathom Analytics
    - text: "is another strong hosted option if you value a clean interface and minimal configuration. Its philosophy is similar to Plausible: privacy-first, cookieless analytics rather than detailed individual tracking. A recent comparison from Matomo places Fathom among the simpler cookieless privacy-focused platforms."
    - link "Analytics Platform - Matomo":
      - /url: https://matomo.org/blog/2026/06/a-hands-on-guide-to-privacy-analytics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Analytics Platform - Matomo
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Tradeoff:"
    - text: you'll give up some of the customization and analytical depth available in Matomo or product-analytics platforms.
  - heading "3. Matomo — when you want more analytical power" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - link "Matomo":
      - /url: https://matomo.org/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - text: Matomo
    - text: is the option I'd investigate if "alternative to GA4" means
    - strong: "\"I want something nearly as capable, but with greater control over my data.\""
    - text: It supports substantially more functionality than lightweight privacy tools and can be self-hosted. Matomo describes its platform as privacy-focused and suitable from small organizations through enterprise.
    - link "Analytics Platform - Matomo":
      - /url: https://matomo.org/blog/2026/06/a-hands-on-guide-to-privacy-analytics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Analytics Platform - Matomo
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Tradeoff:"
    - text: more features mean more configuration and operational overhead. Self-hosting also means you're responsible for infrastructure and updates.
  - heading "4. Umami — excellent for technical/self-hosting teams" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - link "Umami":
      - /url: https://umami.is/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - text: Umami
    - text: is worth shortlisting if your SaaS has developers who are comfortable running infrastructure. It's an open-source, self-hostable approach that gives you considerable control over where analytics data lives. Current comparisons generally position it as a lightweight alternative rather than a full GA4 replacement.
    - link "Measr +1":
      - /url: https://measr.app/compare/privacy-analytics/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Measr
      - generic: "+1"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Tradeoff:"
    - text: the money you save on a hosted analytics subscription can become engineering/maintenance time.
  - heading "5. Simple Analytics — maximum simplicity" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - link "Simple Analytics":
      - /url: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - text: Simple Analytics
    - text: "takes perhaps the most minimalist approach: no cookies, no personal data, and a very straightforward dashboard. It's particularly attractive if you primarily care about aggregate website traffic rather than identifying and analyzing individual visitors."
    - link "Simple Analytics +1":
      - /url: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/google-analytics-alternatives?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Simple Analytics
      - generic: "+1"
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "Tradeoff:"
    - text: that simplicity means less granular behavioral analysis.
  - heading "What I'd shortlist for a small SaaS" [level=3]
  - paragraph:
    - strong: "My order would be:"
  - list:
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Plausible
      - text: — best balance of privacy, simplicity and useful SaaS website metrics.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Matomo
      - text: — if you need substantially more analytical depth.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Fathom
      - text: — if you want the easiest polished hosted experience.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Umami
      - text: — if self-hosting/data ownership is important.
    - paragraph:
      - strong: Simple Analytics
      - text: — if you want analytics to be almost completely "set and forget."
  - paragraph:
    - text: "One important distinction:"
    - strong: website analytics isn't the same as product analytics.
    - text: If your real question is
    - emphasis: "\"Which features do logged-in customers use, where do they drop out of onboarding, and which cohorts retain?\""
    - text: ", I'd also evaluate a product-analytics platform such as PostHog alongside one of the privacy-first website tools. Privacy-focused alternatives deliberately avoid much of the individual-level tracking that makes those analyses possible."
    - link "Simple Analytics":
      - /url: https://www.simpleanalytics.com/google-analytics-alternatives?utm_source=chatgpt.com
      - generic: Simple Analytics
